maya-support: customer says they get a 403 from our API but there's no request/session header in the response. They pasted the error screenshot but no network HAR. asking what to collect for escalation

ravi-eng: quick checklist to request from customer: short curl that reproduces the 403, full response headers (not just message), timestamp (UTC), SDK + version if using an SDK, and a short screen recording or HAR if possible.

maya-support: do we have a tiny copy-paste curl example i can send? i don't want to ask for their API key ofc.

ravi-eng: yep — ask them to copy-as-curl from browser or use this minimal template and redact their key:  

```
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED_API_KEY>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "X-RWI-Session: <leave-empty-if-unknown>" \
  -d '{"input":"hello"}'
```

Replace body with a minimal payload that reproduces the 403. Tell them to paste the exact terminal output (status line + headers + body).

ben-console: if they can't run curl, give this browser HAR quickflow: Network tab -> reproduce -> right-click any request -> Save all as HAR. If they prefer a smaller export, ask for the single failed request -> Copy -> Copy as cURL (then paste) — that includes headers. Important: don't remove header lines except redact Authorization.

ravi-eng: also helpful: find the SDK session id. Web SDK prints session id on init (console) or you can call `RWI.session()` in console to surface it. Mobile SDKs usually expose `sessionId` in their debug logs. Tell the customer to search their logs for "session" around the failure timestamp. Note common header we set: `X-RWI-Session` (if present please include).

maya-support: what if they have no session header and no HAR? customer said their infra strips headers.

ravi-eng: then ask for these extras: (1) exact UTC timestamp of the attempt (yyyy-mm-dd hh:mm:ss), (2) the client IP if they can get it from their server logs, (3) a minimal reproducible payload and the exact endpoint path + method, (4) consent to us pulling a support bundle for that window (we need their account/email). With the timestamp + account we can look up internal logs and correlate.

ben-console: on our side the Console -> Support -> Create support bundle lets you pick time range (we recommend +/- 5 minutes around the timestamp). That bundle includes internal traces and the proxy logs that often show the upstream error code and any stripped headers. Ask them to approve us pulling it, or the customer can export via Account -> Support -> Export debug archive and attach.

maya-support: any privacy/PII reminders i should add?

ravi-eng: yes — ask them to redact any customer PII before posting publicly. If they can't, instruct secure upload (we have a one-time S3 link from Console -> Support) and note retention (we keep bundles for 30 days).

support-bot: automated note: please include these exact fields when creating a ticket: `account_id`, `account_email`, `UTC timestamp`, `endpoint`, `method`, `minimal-curl-output` (headers + body), `session_id_if_any`, `HAR_or_screencap`, `redwood_console_bundle_id_if_submitted`.

maya-support: perfect — i'll DM the customer with the checklist + the curl template and ask for permission to pull a bundle if they can't supply a HAR. :thumbsup:

ravi-eng: thanks — if they give the timestamp ping me and i'll run a quick correlation query on proxy logs.

ben-console: fyi if you need to escalate to infra for header-stripping patterns include `client-ip` and `user-agent` in the ask; that speeds lookup.

maya-support: noted. sending now.
